newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Vietnam seeks to change term Bach Ho crude price.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam seeks to change term Bach Ho crude price.

text.p: State-owned Petrovietnam Trading Co (Petechim) has proposed to its term buyers to change the official selling price (OSP) formula of its Bach Ho crude oil, a company source said on Tuesday.
The change to the term price will include the average spot price of Platt's published assessment, which is not in the current formula.
This is the first time that Petechim is seeking to adjust the Bach Ho OSP since the heavy sweet crude was sold in 1989.
Traders said the change is expected to result in a higher term price, allowing Petechim to raise its revenue.
Petechim will need the agreement of all its term buyers before implementing the new formula, which could force some buyers to end their contracts or reduce the volume, traders said.
However, other buyers could emerge as Bach Ho is considered a good alternative to Indonesia's Minas crude, they said.
The current OSP uses only the monthly average of the bi-weekly price assessment of the Asian Petroleum Price Index (APPI) for Minas crude, and then a premium is added.
The premium is reviewed every six months between Petechim and the term buyers.
The Bach Ho OSP for April to September was set at a premium of 80 cents per barrel to the Minas APPI quotes.
For the new formula, Petechim proposed to take an average of a three-week assessment of the Minas APPI and Platt's Minas daily spot quotes, and add an 85-cent-per-barrel premium.
The addition of Platt's quotes might raise the Bach Ho term price since the bi-weekly APPI assessment was deemed to be below market levels, traders said.
In May, the administrator of APPI sent a letter to its panelists, complaining that the Minas quotes submitted into the APPI were much lower than spot market prices.
The APPI panelists comprise producers, refiners, consumers and traders.
The low Minas APPI and good demand for Bach Ho are propping up the Vietnamese crude's spot premiums to the term price.
In July, Bach Ho traded on the spot market at 40 cents per barrel premium to the OSP.
Bach Ho term contracts are reviewed every six months, and talks for the October to April contracts started this week.
Petechim sells the bulk of its 170,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) Bach Ho crude output by term deals.
Shell has the largest term volume for Bach Ho at around 40,000 bpd, Exxon and Caltex each lifts around 5,000 bpd, while Mobil takes 10,000 bpd.

Trading houses Sumitomo Corp, Nissho Iwai and Mitsubishi Corp are the biggest Japanese lifters, taking 20,000 bpd. Marubeni Corp, Mitsui 8031.T), Kanematsu Corp 8020.T and China's Unipec each takes 5,000 bpd.

Traders said if the new formula was introduced, it could prompt some western buyers to terminate their contracts. "But there will probably be new buyers who are willing to try the crude, despite the higher term price," a Japanese trader said.
Traders also said they expected the Japanese trading houses holding the larger term volumes to cut their volumes, although those taking 5,000 bpd may continue.
But a Japanese trader with a 5,000-bpd contract said: "If the term price is increased, we will definitely withdraw."
-- Singapore Newsroom (+65 870 3082)
